'''Hitaka Shrine''' (日高神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Mizusawa|en|Mizusawa|qid=Q1114302|lt=Mizusawa, Ōshū, Iwate|1=Mizusawa}}, {{ill|Ōshū, Iwate|en|Ōshū, Iwate|qid=Q386052|lt=Ōshū, Iwate|1=Ōshū, Iwate}}, {{ill|Iwate Prefecture|en|Iwate Prefecture|qid=Q48326|lt=Iwate Prefecture|1=Iwate Prefecture}}. It was classified as a former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|qid=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|qid=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|qq=ja_comment|qid=Q134917316|qq= 近代社格制度}}.
The shrine is known for its {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|qid=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}}-designated main hall and the {{ill|Hitaka Hibuse Festival|ja|日高火防祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hitaka Hibuse Festival|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 日高火防祭り|1=Hitaka Hibuse Festival|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11510844}}.
== Name ==
[[File:日高神社参道.JPG|thumb|right|200px|The sacred forest and the approach to Hitaka Shrine]]
The origin of the shrine's name has multiple theories. One suggests that the area was historically known as {{ill|Hitakami|en|Hitakami|qid=Q11288931|lt=Hitakami no Kuni|1=Hitakami}} and served as a central location for its people. Another tradition states that during the {{ill|Former Nine Years' War|en|Former Nine Years' War|qid=Q1187448|lt=Former Nine Years' War|1=Former Nine Years' War}}, {{ill|Minamoto no Yoriyoshi|en|Minamoto no Yoriyoshi|qid=Q3082851|lt=Minamoto no Yoriyoshi|1=Minamoto no Yoriyoshi}} prayed at this shrine, and soon after, the rain ceased, the sun rose high in the sky, and by the Hour of the Goat (around 2 PM), he successfully defeated {{ill|Abe no Sadato|en|Abe no Sadato|qid=Q3616500|lt=Abe no Sadatō|1=Abe no Sadato}}.
The shrine is also referred to as "Hitaka Myōken" or "Hitaka Myōken-gū" due to its association with {{ill|Myōken|en|Myōken|qid=Q10960623|lt=Myōken|1=Myōken}}, a Buddhist deity.
== Deities ==
The shrine enshrines the following eight deities:
* {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en|Ame-no-Minakanushi|qid=Q2842779|lt=Ame-no-Minakanushi|1=Ame-no-Minakanushi}}
* {{ill|Kagu-tsuchi|ja|火産霊神|1=Kagu-tsuchi|lt=Kagutsuchi|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagu-tsuchi|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagutsuchi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to カグツチ}}
* {{ill|Toshigami|lt=Ōtoshi-no-Kami|ja|大年神|1=Toshigami|lt=Ōtoshi-no-kami|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toshigami|13=User:Immanuelle/Toshigami|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to QID FIXED|qid=Q3028663}}
* {{ill|Mitoshi-no-Kami|ja|御年神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mitoshi-no-Kami|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to QID FIXED|qid=Q3028663|1=Toshigami|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q3028663}}
* Wakatoshi-no-Kami
* {{ill|Mizuhanome|lt=Mizuha-no-Me|ja|水波能売神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mizuhanome|qid=Q8191796}}
* {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大国主神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|qid=Q276944}}
* {{ill|Ukanomitama|ja|倉稲魂神|1=Ukanomitama|2=ja|3=倉稲魂神|4=de|5=Ukanomitama|6=eo|7=Ukanomitama|8=mni|9=ꯎꯀꯅꯣꯃꯤꯇꯃ|10=ru|11=Ука-но_митама|12=simple|13=Ukanomitama|14=sv|15=Ukanomitama|16=zh|17=宇迦之御魂神|qid=Q3080728|lt=Ukanomitama|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ukanomitama|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ウカノミタマ}}
Ame-no-Minakanushi is frequently syncretized with {{ill|Myōken|en|Myōken|qid=Q10960623|lt=Myōken|1=Myōken}}.
== History ==
=== Founding Legend ===
According to tradition, Hitaka Shrine was established in the 1st year of the {{ill|Kōnin (era)|en|Kōnin (era)|qid=Q1373070|lt=Kōnin era|1=Kōnin (era)}} (810) by imperial decree of {{ill|Emperor Saga|en|Emperor Saga|qid=Q316654|lt=Emperor Saga|1=Emperor Saga}}. This event occurred eight years after the submission of {{ill|Aterui|en|Aterui|qid=Q1088046|lt=Aterui|1=Aterui}} and the construction of {{ill|Isawa Castle|en|Isawa Castle|qid=Q11611683|lt=Fort Isawa|1=Isawa Castle}} by {{ill|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|en|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|qid=Q941979|lt=Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|1=Sakanoue no Tamuramaro}} in 802. It is believed that the shrine was created as part of the central government's efforts to integrate local beliefs with those of the Yamato court.
=== Heian Period and Beyond ===
The shrine was visited for battle prayers by {{ill|Minamoto no Yoriyoshi|en|Minamoto no Yoriyoshi|qid=Q3082851|lt=Minamoto no Yoriyoshi|1=Minamoto no Yoriyoshi}} and his son {{ill|Minamoto no Yoshiie|en|Minamoto no Yoshiie|qid=Q32613|lt=Minamoto no Yoshiie|1=Minamoto no Yoshiie}} during both the {{ill|Former Nine Years' War|en|Former Nine Years' War|qid=Q1187448|lt=Former Nine Years' War|1=Former Nine Years' War}} and the {{ill|Gosannen War|en|Gosannen War|qid=Q1187411|lt=Later Three Years' War|1=Gosannen War}}. It was also revered by the {{ill|Izawa clan|ja|伊沢氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izawa clan|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 留守氏|1=Rusu clan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q2975345}}, the {{ill|Northern Fujiwara|en|Northern Fujiwara|qid=Q1050942|lt=Northern Fujiwara|1=Northern Fujiwara}}, and later by the {{ill|Date clan|en|Date clan|qid=Q1151061|lt=Date clan|1=Date clan}}.
In 1170 (2nd year of {{ill|Kaō (era)|en|Kaō (era)|qid=Q1150842|lt=Kaō era|1=Kaō (era)}}), {{ill|Fujiwara no Hidehira|en|Fujiwara no Hidehira|qid=Q3090625|lt=Fujiwara no Hidehira|1=Fujiwara no Hidehira}} sponsored the reconstruction of the shrine.<ref>‘''Rikuchū Province Isawa District Village Records''’ (陸中国胆沢郡村誌, 1880). Notably, this was the same year Hidehira was appointed Chinjufu-shōgun (鎮守府将軍).</ref> During the late 16th century, {{ill|Date Masamune|en|Date Masamune|qid=Q311183|lt=Date Masamune|1=Date Masamune}} contributed to its rebuilding and granted shrine lands. In 1632 (9th year of {{ill|Kan'ei|en|Kan'ei|qid=Q1192913|lt=Kan'ei era|1=Kan'ei}}), {{ill|Lusumune Tadayoshi|ja|留守宗利|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Lusumune Tadayoshi|1=Date Munetosi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11237935}}, the first lord of {{ill|Mizusawa Castle|ja|水沢城|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mizusawa Castle|1=Mizusawa Castle|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11548846}}, ordered the reconstruction of the main shrine building.
=== Modern Era ===
In 1869 (2nd year of {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era|1=Meiji era}}), Hitaka Shrine became the general shrine of {{ill|Isawa Prefecture|ja|胆沢県|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isawa Prefecture|1=Isawa Prefecture|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11611687}}. In 1874, it was designated as a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|qid=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|qid=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|qq=ja_comment|qid=Q134917316|qq= 近代社格制度}} (a significant local shrine). This Ranking system was abolished in 1946.
== Shrine Buildings ==
The main shrine building, constructed in 1632, features a three-bay {{ill|Nagare-zukuri|en|Nagare-zukuri|qid=Q210684|lt=Nagare-zukuri|1=Nagare-zukuri}} style with a copper roof. It was designated an {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|qid=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}} in 1990 for its unique Edo-period architectural features.<ref>[http://www.bunka.pref.iwate.jp/ciss/bunkazai/detail/id/33 Iwate Prefecture Cultural Heritage Database - Hitaka Shrine Main Hall]</ref>
